title: Sofacy_Backdoor_Investigation_914
description: Investigate a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes
Analyze network traffic for signs of C2 communication

levels.title: Scenario Background
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis backdoor is known for its modular architecture and capabilities for command-and-control (C2) communication, exfiltration, and persistence.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the `target` host via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Access the `target` host via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the `target` host. Your task is to identify and investigate any unauthorized or suspicious services running on this host. Look for a service named `c2-listener.service`.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, start by listing all services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any services that are not part of the standard system services. Specifically, identify the service named `c2-listener.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding what constitutes a suspicious service. Look for services that are not part of the standard system services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to list all running services and inspect them for any that seem out of place.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a service named `c2-listener.service` which is not a standard system service and is likely the suspicious service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service on the `target` host. Your next step is to determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication. Look for port `80`.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for the suspicious communication, use the command `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to inspect active connections. Look for the port number `80` used by the suspicious service. This port is commonly used for HTTP traffic but could be misused for C2 communication.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand that C2 communication often uses specific ports. Look for ports that are commonly used for such communication.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use commands like `netstat -tuln`, `ss -tuln`, or `lsof -i` to inspect active connections and identify the port used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for connections on port `80` which is commonly used for HTTP traffic but could be misused for C2 communication.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: You suspect that the attacker may have moved laterally from the `target` host to the `next-target` host. Your task is to identify any file transfers or remote execution used to move between these hosts. Look for the service `payload-transfer.service`.
levels.solution: To investigate lateral movement, use the command `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` to inspect logs for evidence of file transfers or remote execution involving `payload-transfer.service`. Look for any unusual entries in the logs that indicate file transfers or remote execution commands.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand that lateral movement often involves file transfers or remote execution. Look for evidence of these activities.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use commands like `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` to inspect logs for evidence of file transfers or remote execution.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for any unusual entries in the logs that indicate file transfers or remote execution commands, specifically involving `payload-transfer.service`.
